reference: Lionel Levine and Yuval Peres, 'Strong spherical asymptotics for rotor-router aggregation and the divisible sandpile', Potential Analysis 30, 1 (2009), is the theorem this plate measures. For an aggregate of n particles in d dimensions, written as n = ω_d r^d, they prove the inradius is at least r − O(log r) and the outradius at most r + O(r^α) for every α > 1 − 1/d, which in the plane is r + O(r^α) for every α > 1/2. The two sides of that sandwich are not the same strength, and the plate does not pretend they are: the inner bound is logarithmic and proved, the outer bound proved here is a power, and the status line reports what this lattice actually measures rather than what the tighter of the two would suggest. There is no probability anywhere in the statement. The rotor-router walk and the aggregation model are James Propp's; they are studied in Ander Holroyd and James Propp, 'Rotor walks and Markov chains', Contemporary Mathematics 520 (2010), and in Joshua Cooper and Joel Spencer, 'Simulating a random walk with constant error', Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 15 (2006). reference: Three-vortex collapse bound: an explicit formula and sharp minimum for a classical three-vortex collapse family, independently derived in this project with AI assistance. Fluids 22, 057104 (2010), gives rotation and collapse separately and writes their product as the pitch of the log spiral. Jpn. 56, 2024 (1987), section 4, gives the collapse and rotation rates A and B in this same parametrization, for circulations (2, 2, −1), and their ratio B/(−2A) is this formula; he minimizes the collision time instead, at cos 2θ = 3/5, where the product is 3/2, the value it also takes at θ = 45°. reference: A closed form and sharp minimum for the scale-invariant product on a classical five-vortex collapse family, independently derived in this project with AI assistance. Circulations Γ = (−1, −1, 1/2, 1/2, −3/4), four vortices at the vertices of a parallelogram whose diagonals meet at the fifth, diagonals in ratio 1/√2, angle θ between the diagonals, 0 < θ < π/2. ω₀ t_c = (3/16)(7 − 4 cos 2θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ 3√33/16, equality uniquely at cos 2θ = 4/7. With φ = 2θ the quotient is (7 − 4 cos φ)/sin φ, and the critical point is cos φ = 4/7. Five-vortex parallelogram-plus-center collapse is Novikov and Sedov, Sov. Phys. JETP 50, 297 (1979). Gotoda, arXiv:2002.09624 (2020 preprint), eq. (3.13), gives the collapse rate A(θ) and the spin B(θ) separately after those authors, and plots this family (γ1 = −1, γ2 = 1/2, γ3 = −3/4) as Hamiltonian against collapse rate. The product −B/(2A) on that slice simplifies to the formula above. The formula and minimum were derived here and recorded on 2026-09-20. Historical priority is unconfirmed; see identities/NOVELTY-AUDIT.md and IDENTITIES.md. The reciprocal pair with the diagonals swapped is the same family. If the vortices leave the quincunx, or the kernel is wrong, the ratio against 3√33/16 misses and the status line marks miss. The picture still draws. This is not Novikov and Sedov's t_* or ω separately under a new name, and it is not the four-vortex parallelogram lock.
